OS DataMercs
OS DataMercs is a metadata consultancy for scholarly publishing and libraries: standards-first, practical, and allergic to hype. We consult, teach, and help ship discovery-grade metadata — MARC21, ONIX, KBART, JATS/BITS — including how to record AI contribution without breaking the catalogue.
Services
Consulting
Architecture and governance for product data and bibliographic metadata: modelling guidelines, quality processes, partner feeds, and ERP-to-discovery pipelines.
Teaching
Workshops and guided practice for editorial, data, and library teams — usable the same week, not slide-deck tourism.
Delivery
Hands-on metadata products and tooling support: audits, enrichment rules, KBART/MARC/ONIX delivery hygiene, provenance patterns for AI-assisted works.
Olaf Schmalfuß
Librarian by training (M.A. Library and Information Science & German Linguistics, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin) and data practitioner by trade. Since 2012 at De Gruyter Brill in Berlin — Technical Customer Service leadership, then Product Data, Metadata & Standards: product data warehouse, data governance & stewardship, Klopotek/SAP interfaces, and partner metadata (GBV, OCLC, EBSCO, Ex Libris, and others).
Earlier: book trade and the library of the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science.
Contact: os@datamercs.net · datamercs.net · LinkedIn · GitHub · ORCID

articles.title: BISAC 2025 → Thema 1.6
articles.description: Official EDItEUR mapping, with heuristic DDC, LCSH and GND. A tools page — not the shop-window face.
articles.contents:
A lookup for subject schemes, not a catalogue of titles. BISAC 2025 → Thema 1.6 is the public EDItEUR / BISG mapping (source of truth). DDC, LCSH and GND are heuristics for internal use — useful to steer a classifier, not a WebDewey licence.
The interactive table uses the tools chrome. Open it here:
